faq-item.faq-q: Is LlamaIndex better than LangChain for RAG?
faq-item.faq-a: For pure RAG over document corpora, LlamaIndex generally offers faster hierarchical index retrieval and lower memory overhead out of the box. For RAG as part of a broader agent system, LangChain remains stronger. In 2026, the hybrid pattern (LlamaIndex retrieval wrapped as a LangGraph tool) is the most production-proven.

faq-item.faq-q: Can you build with both frameworks in one project?
faq-item.faq-a: Yes, this is the most common production pattern I build in 2026: LlamaIndex handling retrieval (for speed and low memory) wrapped as a tool inside a LangGraph agent for orchestration. This combines strengths rather than forcing one framework to do both.

faq-item.faq-q: How do you decide which framework to recommend?
faq-item.faq-a: Based on where your hardest problem lives: if it's retrieval quality, latency, or memory over a messy corpus, LlamaIndex. If it's multi-step agent behavior, tool use, or memory, LangChain/LangGraph. The recommendation is delivered in writing with reasoning, before any build work.

faq-item.faq-q: Do I need a LangChain agency or can a freelance consultant handle this?
faq-item.faq-a: Most RAG and agent projects, a specific pipeline, agent, or integration, are well within scope for a single experienced developer. An agency's advantage shows up on large multi-disciplinary product builds needing several specialists in parallel.

faq-item.faq-q: How much does RAG framework development cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A framework selection consultation runs $500 to $1,500. A full LlamaIndex or LangChain build ranges from $8,000 to $30,000+ depending on complexity. A hybrid architecture combining both frameworks typically runs $15,000 to $40,000+. Contact for a fixed-price estimate specific to your use case.
